macro_context.market_sentiment: Mixed-to-cautiously-bullish: S&P 500 and Nasdaq recovered on May 5 (+0.7% / +1% intraday ATH) after a sharp sell-off on May 4 (Dow -1.13%, S&P -0.41%) triggered by Middle East escalation and an oil price spike above $102/bbl. Solid earnings from several companies are providing a near-term offset to geopolitical drag.
macro_context.fed_outlook: FOMC held rates at 3.5%-3.75% on April 29, 2026 in an unusually divided 8-4 vote (Powell's likely final meeting as chair). One dissenter wanted a 25bp cut; three opposed easing-bias language. Market pricing: zero cuts in 2026, one 25bp cut in December 2027. Fed leadership transition adds uncertainty.
macro_context.geopolitical: Active U.S.-Iran conflict is the dominant risk: Iran launched missiles and drones at the UAE and targeted a ship in the Strait of Hormuz after a brief ceasefire expired, driving oil above $102/bbl. Additional flashpoints include U.S.-Venezuela tensions and NATO posture in Greenland. Residual tariff uncertainty continues to cloud the global trade outlook.

web_context.competitor_activity: Meta is on track to surpass Google in global digital ad revenue in 2026 ($243B vs $239B projected). Instagram Reels continues to battle TikTok and YouTube Shorts for short-form video dominance; ad impression growth of 19% YoY and avg price-per-ad up 12% signal Meta is winning ad wallet share. Snap swung to Q1 profit ($45M) but remains far smaller and more exposed to geopolitical ad-budget caution. Smaller peers (Snap, Pinterest) are expected to lose ad share to Meta and Google in uncertain macro environments, which is a relative positive for Meta.
